concerns.text: Task T009 restricts generation to 'TinyLlama-1.1B' exclusively for CI, but spec.md US-1 and FR-001 explicitly require generation across 'two open-source LLM checkpoints'. The task silently weakens the requirement to a single model, violating the spec's core data acquisition scope.

Task T011 mandates generating a control corpus using 'datasets.load_dataset("arxiv_nlp")'. The spec.md and plan.md contain no requirement for a control group or this specific dataset. This introduces an unmandated experimental condition, violating the constraint that tasks must not silently relax or expand the spec's defined scope.

Task T014 implements consistency checks using 'cross-encoder/stsb-distilroberta-base' (a Semantic Textual Similarity model). Spec.md FR-003 and Constitution Principle VI explicitly require a 'Natural Language Inference (NLI) model' to detect 'contradiction'. Using an STS model fails to satisfy the specific semantic constraint of the FR.

Tasks T010 and T013 (retry logic and timeout handling) are marked as incomplete/failed. Spec.md FR-001 explicitly mandates 'retry up to 3 times' as a functional requirement. The absence of a verified task artifact for this logic leaves a critical functional requirement unimplemented.

Tasks T034-T044 implement 'Review-Driven Enhancements' based on simulated reviewer comments (Turing, Rockmore, etc.) but have no traceable link to any Functional Requirement (FR) or Success Criterion (SC) in spec.md. This constitutes unapproved scope creep, violating the constraint that tasks must not introduce features not demanded by the spec.

Task ID T020 is duplicated with conflicting descriptions: one for 'validity_justification.py' (FR-009) and one for 'rubric.md' creation (FR-010). This ID collision indicates a breakdown in task management that risks leaving distinct requirements (FR-009 and FR-010) unimplemented or conflated.
